caption.text:
Sometimes the people who hurt us the most didn’t feel wrong in the beginning. They felt familiar. They felt exciting. They felt like chemistry. But often what we call “chemistry” is simply our nervous system recognizing patterns it learned long before we understood what love was supposed to feel like. When inconsistency, emotional distance, or chaos were once part of what we experienced as connection, our bodies can begin to mistake those things for passion. And so the wrong person can feel right — not because they are good for us, but because they are recognizable. 

Healing begins when we start questioning those patterns. When we realize that love was never meant to feel like anxiety, confusion, or constant uncertainty. Real love is steady. It is calm. It is consistent. And sometimes, when we are used to chaos, that calm can feel unfamiliar at first. But unfamiliar does not mean wrong — it often means healthy. 

Learning to choose differently requires retraining your nervous system, rewriting the story of what love should look like, and allowing yourself to believe that you deserve something softer, safer, and more secure than what you once accepted. The right person will not feel like a rollercoaster. They will feel like peace. 

📖 This reflection was inspired by the book ‘Detached’ by Sabrina Bendory, a powerful exploration of emotional patterns, healing, and learning to recognize the difference between familiarity and real love. 🖤
